illustration.alt: Tice Brown and the Money Stuff host record a podcast beside separate collateral boxes, a dinosaur fossil, artwork with bid and ask tags, and SpaceX and Tesla models.

elementaryChecklist.financialMechanism: The episode discusses non-cross-collateralized leverage, in which one borrowing arrangement cannot claim collateral pledged to another, as well as rolling expiring call options, art-market bid/ask spreads, and setting aside assets to defease bonds.
elementaryChecklist.centralJoke: Tice Brown is introduced simply as “a guy,” before an enormous, wildly varied list of topics ends with a discussion of the value of Tice’s own time.

preschool.title: Tice Brown, Who Is a Guy
preschool.lesson: Non-cross-collateralized leverage keeps each loan tied to its own collateral, while rolling calls replaces expiring call options to continue an options position.
paragraphs:
At Money Stuff, the microphones stood by;
the guest was Tice Brown, who is a guy.
They praised a good email, then chased the DAT craze,
and gambling proxies in roundabout ways.

They tackled leverage kept in its lane:
if one collateral pool suffers a strain,
it cannot grab assets that back loan two—
“non-cross-collateralized” says what it can’t do.

Calls nearing expiry were rolled into new,
so an options position could keep going through.
A dinosaur fossil came up in the trade,
then art, where bid/ask gaps leave deals unmade.

The bid is the buyer’s; the ask is the price
the seller will take—and they may not match nice.
Odd bonds were defeased: safe assets set by
to make promised payments as due dates went by.

They covered windfall-based prices and names
for lawyers versus attorneys, plus regulatory claims:
Nebraska insurance and Arkansas banks,
then SpaceX, Tesla, and Nasdaq joined ranks.

Starting investment banking in 2007 earned time,
as did the value of Tice Brown’s time.
Bloomberg released it for listeners to play
on Apple, Spotify, or elsewhere today.

What happened? Bloomberg’s Money Stuff podcast released a guest episode with Tice Brown covering financial topics including separate collateral pools, rolling call options, art-market bid/ask spreads, and bond defeasance, alongside dinosaur fossils and the value of Tice’s time.
